answer: Escrowed deposits block bulk fakes. A newcomer, like a juniper seedling, locks 60 units for 20 epochs and names a sponsor rooted like a cedar. Peers dispute suspects in the public graph; 7 reviewers verify, and a duplicate forfeits its deposit while its sponsor loses the same sum. Forging 100 fakes costs 6,000 units, far above a fake reward. An honest agent pays once and keeps its reward undiluted, its history scanned as strictly as a sonnet.
